tasks.label: Install extension (.vsix)

windows.command: code --uninstall-extension local.ghcp-usage-metrics 2>$null; code --install-extension (Get-ChildItem '${workspaceFolder}/extension/*.vsix' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName --force; $keep = ((Get-Content "$HOME/.vscode/extensions/extensions.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json) | Where-Object { $_.identifier.id -eq 'local.ghcp-usage-metrics' }).location.path -replace '.*/',''; Get-ChildItem "$HOME/.vscode/extensions" -Directory -Filter 'local.ghcp-usage-metrics-*' | Where-Object { $_.Name -ne $keep } | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

tasks.detail: Uninstall any existing build first, then install the newest .vsix. Installing over the top leaves one orphaned folder per version, and after a downgrade VS Code can load the wrong one.
